competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move under the trusted duration-1 P&L convention. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: Overnight trading leaned dovish on policy forwards even as oil, the dollar, and long-end yields kept the macro backdrop restrictive. SOFR and CORRA March 2027 implieds fell to 4.485% and 2.945% from prior marks near 4.625% and 3.09%, while the US 10-year eased five basis points to 5.24% but remains near multi-decade highs. Brent held near $102 and WTI near $93, gold above $4,200, equities firm with the S&P at 7,666, and VIX at 16.3. Euro-area inflation surprised hot, yet widening sovereign spreads have markets betting the ECB delivers fewer hikes. USDCAD sits at 1.42 in the top percentile of its one-year range. Next focus: whether the STIR rally persists, which ECB story dominates, and whether elevated long yields begin to stress AI capex and the consumer.

postmortems.what_worked: The exit correctly named the economic identity: cash 2.30 versus contract 3.09 and a SOFR charge of 3.88 meant the CAD receive was a path-premium fade, not a cash-carry harvest.
postmortems.what_failed: Flattening at 3.09 for a 1bp scratch left the subsequent 14.5bp contract decline on the table if the trigger was ordinary oil-beta backup rather than a cash-policy shift.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The original carry label was wrong at entry. The close captured that diagnosis but, if oil-beta was the trigger, violated the hold-through-ordinary-variance rule.
postmortems.expression_assessment: A CAD March 2027 receive versus cash 2.30 was never a carry vehicle. Repair is expression selection, not nostalgia for reopening CAD.

causal.original_belief: CAD March 2027 receive was booked as a holdable rates expression; cash then 2.30 versus contract 3.10 meant the economic identity was a fade of hike and path premium, not a cash-carry harvest, and the recorded SOFR charge of 3.88 made CAD a negative-carry leg versus USD funding.
causal.observed_reality: The receive was flattened at 3.09 for a 1bp scratch. After the exit, CORRA March 2027 marked 2.945 versus cash 2.31, so the contract fell another 14.5bp and path premium compressed from about 79bp at exit to about 63.5bp now. Cash-policy did not shift enough to justify flattening.
causal.assumptions_right: The carry diagnosis at exit was economically correct: the instrument was path premium, not coupon. Cash stayed near 2.30 to 2.31, so the identity never became a positive-carry hold versus USD.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: A small oil-beta backup was treated as permission to flatten a still-working path fade. Once owned, a CAD receive should not be flattened on ordinary oil-sensitive variance; invalidate only on cash-policy shift or a large persistent path reprice higher.
causal.causal_divergence: Invalidation hygiene, not a failed carry engine. Two facts can both be true: the seat should not have owned this as a carry trade, and once owned it should not have been flattened on small oil-beta backup. The close captured the first fact and violated the second if oil was the trigger.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: Respecting the active lesson would have kept the receive through ordinary oil-beta variance and harvested the subsequent 14.5bp contract decline. It would not have rewritten the instrument into a positive-carry hold versus USD. Correct future behavior is keep a CAD receive only when the expression is carry-valid, then exit only on cash-policy shift or large persistent path reprice.
causal.future_implication: Do not reopen CORRA March 2027 receive while 2.945 versus cash 2.31 is still about 63.5bp of path premium. Apply the do-not-flatten-on-oil-beta rule only to carry-valid CAD receives.

postmortems.no_new_lesson: No new lesson. Realized 1bp versus the subsequent 3.09 to 2.945 move is bounded ordinary variance around the already-active rule: do not flatten a CAD receive on a small oil-beta backup; invalidate only on cash-policy shift or large persistent path reprice. Process remains sound if that rule is applied to carry-valid CAD receives and CAD is not reopened while it is still a path-premium fade.

Brent near 102 is the live hawkish-Canada risk, but the accepted expanding clips are too small to hedge that path or to add a second independent macro bet. Unused risk capacity is not a reason to overlay token AONIA, US 10-year, or CAD FX risk that either duplicates easing beta or only partially offsets it.
pragmatist.invalidation: CORRA March 2027 implied back through 3.13, or cash CORRA reversing higher toward 2.70-plus with a clear Bank of Canada hike path led by oil or inflation; either event ends the hold and forces a cut or exit.

expression_memo.rationale: No incremental rates or spot risk; managing the current book only.

portfolio_construction.existing_book_summary: Single live line: long/receive 450 million CORRA March 2027, entry 3.13, implied 2.945, shocked risk capital 4.5 million versus the hard stop. The book is a Canada-easing / overpriced-hike-path expression versus 2.31 cash CORRA.

independent_handoff_opportunities.rationale: Cross-merchant expanding long 15 million at 110.90. Independent CAD versus JPY mark; would add FX risk, not another CORRA line.
Carry-is-king expanding receive 25 million, mark 4.83 versus cash AONIA 4.60. Independent AUD March 2027 implied versus cash.
Perma-bear expanding long 25 million, mark 5.24. Independent US long-end cash yield, distinct tenor and sovereign from CORRA March 2027.
Positioning-cynic expanding short 15 million at 1.4246. Independent CAD versus USD mark; trader holds include the opposite USDCAD long.

portfolio_construction.adverse_scenario: Oil-led Canada reacceleration: Brent stays bid, CAD firms, Bank of Canada reprices hikes, and CORRA March 2027 implied rises back through 3.13. That is a rates selloff in the existing receive, not a slow grind.

candidate_interactions.rationale: Long CADJPY tends to win in a hawkish, oil-strong CAD path that hurts the CORRA receive, and lose in the dovish CAD path that pays the receive. Residual JPY beta makes the offset impure.
Another G10 policy-rate receive. Helps in global easing and hurts in global reacceleration alongside the CAD line rather than hedging it.
Long US duration is still rates-down beta in the global disinflation state that already pays the book. Country and tenor differ, but the book's main adverse path hits both.
Short USDCAD is long CAD FX and would offset a hawkish-Canada shock to the receive. Same CAD-FX direction as long CADJPY; stacking them would duplicate FX beta.

portfolio_construction.chosen_actions_rationale: Hold the working 450 million CORRA receive. Cash is still 2.31, the line is through entry, and Canada-US yield divergence remains the clean opportunistic expression. The four expanding clips are token versus 450 million and do not change shocked P&L in the oil/US-spillover scenario.

rejected_complements.reason: Fifteen million is a token impure hedge of the oil/hawkish-Canada path; JPY risk-off beta can lose while the receive wins, and size cannot offset material CORRA P&L.
Duplicate G10 easing beta at token 25 million. A clip that does not change book risk does not earn a seat.
Twenty-five million of US duration does not diversify the adverse inflation path and is too small to be a second swing.
Token 15 million CAD-FX offset with a conflicting trader hold on USDCAD long. Would not hedge 450 million of CORRA.

grinder.thesis: The book stays flat. None of the four markable expanding handoffs shows expected edge large enough to pay official SOFR 3.90 ACT/360 charged on shocked-risk capital after a 100bp rate shock or a 1 percent spot shock. Cash-versus-strip gaps and outright yield levels are priced paths, not alpha, and the FX sleeves have no stated target that covers a 1 percent adverse move.
grinder.invalidation: A later frozen markable candidate with a quantified expected P&L that exceeds SOFR on the same 100bp or 1 percent shocked-capital path, and with a catalyst consistent with the required mark direction, would reopen deployment at a reduced size.

deployment_hurdle.benchmark: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 3.90% as of 2026-09-30 charged on shocked-risk capital; stay flat if expected edge does not cover that charge after a plausible adverse 100bp rate move or 1 percent spot move.

candidate_assessments.rationale: Long 15 million at 110.90 is markable. A 1 percent adverse spot move is about 0.15 million shocked capital, but no expected directional edge or target is given to pay official SOFR on that stock. Preservation sizing from the 1 percent path leaves an uncompensated hole versus an unspecified expected P&L.
